title: Econ Lighthouse: Runway Savings Initiative for Batching, KV-prefetch, and Quant Profiles
creator: Jared Kim
description: Objective: Deliver a tightly scoped initiative that demonstrates predictable per-token cost reductions (target: 15–25% on median workloads) without degrading quality beyond defined thresholds. Scope: coordinated experiments and rollouts across three levers — continuous batching defaults, adaptive KV-prefetch (prefix caching), and conservative quantization profiles — for hosted and dedicated tiers. Success metrics: 1) 15%+ effective unit cost reduction across sampled real traffic within 6 weeks of rollout; 2) <1.5% quality regression on core prompt suites (measured by eval harness); 3) No customer-facing latency SLO breaches >1% of requests during rollout. Deliverables: 1) experiment matrix and hypothesis tracker; 2) dashboard with token-econ, latency, and quality signals per route/model; 3) rollout policy templates (canary, gradual, automatic rollback); 4) playbook for customer communications and opt-out controls. Timeline & milestones: - Week 0 (Jan 20): kickoff, baseline telemetry capture completed. - Week 2 (Feb 3): engineering spike: batching + prefetched KV prototype landed (spike branch + perf harness). - Week 4 (Feb 17): first closed field trial on low-risk customer cohort (10% traffic) for batching-only config. - Week 6 (Mar 3): combine batching + KV-prefetch + conservative quant profiles in sandbox for A/B trials. - Week 8 (Mar 17): analyze results, validate quality/econ thresholds, prepare rollout. - Week 12 (Apr 18): targeted rollout to hosted tier with canary progression. Guardrails & acceptance: - Quality regression threshold: absolute drop <= 1.5% on evaluation SLOs; if exceeded, abort and revert. - Latency target: P95 increase <= 20ms for latency-sensitive routes; unexpected latency raises automated rollback. - Observability: per-route token cost, KV hit-rate, batch-size distribution, and model output quality must be visible in Console. Risks & mitigations: - GPU capacity constraints: coordinate with infra (ENG) to reserve burst capacity for trials. - Regressions from quantization: run automated eval suite + holdout human review for high-risk routes. - Customer opt-out: provide per-customer flag and disable-by-default for enterprise customers. Dependencies: runtime-1.19 kernel selection changes (ENG- dependency), Console rollout for new dashboards, and Billing metrics pipeline update. Notes: keep conservative defaults and make aggressive knobs opt-in. This initiative is explicitly experimental: we prioritize safe measurable savings over aggressive, global defaults.
